text: Browsers remember your tabs. They do not remember your intent. For someone with attention or working memory difficulties, a small interruption can mean starting an entire task again. Hold My Place is a private browser extension that leaves one clear next step for your return.

Here is the working prototype. This is a practice licence renewal, with five steps and made up details. I complete my details and address, then reach the photo step. The application stays in my browser. Nothing is submitted.

Now an interruption arrives. I hold my place, then step away. When I return, there is a short reminder: complete the photo. Continue takes me straight to the field and highlights it. There is less to reconstruct, and no pressure to hurry.

The capture is visible. It records labels and whether fields are filled, never the answers I typed. A personal note can replace an unhelpful cue. Read aloud is optional. If I am finished, Forget everything removes the saved place. Control stays with the person.

Cloudflare Workers hosts the demo and an optional AI endpoint. Before an AI request, you can inspect the exact metadata that will be sent. Workers AI turns that structure into a short cue. If the service fails, the local rule based cue remains available. No cloud database stores your places.

This is also a real Chrome and Edge extension. On ordinary websites, use Alt H or the toolbar button. The return banner offers Continue and Done. The places list lets you inspect the capture, edit a note, and delete it. Captures expire after twenty four hours by default.

Settings offer text, spoken cues, and configurable expiry. Cloud AI is off by default. Sensitive page detection blocks likely banking, health and payment pages from using AI. A focused submit or pay button produces a check first warning. These safeguards help, but cannot guarantee that every page or AI cue is correct.

Hold My Place is a solo project for the accessibility and disability inclusion track. This example evaluation uses clearly labeled synthetic data, not real participants. It illustrates how we will measure completion, time to resume, effort, and cue accuracy. Real participant validation is next. A pause should not mean starting over.
